definitions.explanation: A person one does not know or has never met. The classical negative form ぬ gives the expression a slightly literary quality.

examples.japanese: {見知|みし}らぬ{人|ひと}に{声|こえ}をかけられた。
{見知|みし}らぬ{人|ひと}についていってはいけません。
{電車|でんしゃ}の{中|なか}で{見知|みし}らぬ{人|ひと}に{親切|しんせつ}にしてもらった。
examples.english: A stranger was kind to me on the train.

notes:
Uses the classical negative auxiliary ぬ (attached to the verb {見知|みし}る, "to know by sight"), which is preserved as a fixed expression in modern Japanese. Sounds slightly more literary or formal than {知|し}らない{人|ひと}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見知|みし}らぬ{人|ひと}に{声|こえ}をかけられる: to be spoken to by a stranger
- {見知|みし}らぬ{土地|とち}: unfamiliar land
- {見知|みし}らぬ{顔|かお}: an unfamiliar face
- {見知|みし}らぬ{番号|ばんごう}: an unknown number

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {知|し}らない{人|ひと}: someone you don't know — the everyday, conversational equivalent
- {他人|たにん}: other person; stranger — emphasizes social distance or non-relation
- {赤|あか}の{他人|たにん}: a complete stranger — emphatic form stressing total lack of connection
